messages:
anya: FYI our launch posts went live 07:05 PT. GA shows +2.8k sessions but Pulseboard only shows 54 conversions for the launch page. that feels off. anyone noticing conversion delta? :eyes:

felix: saw the spike. initial hunch: link shortener or redirect chain stripping utm params. we used link.ly for some cross-posts.

jamie: can we segment by referral_domain and click_id? might reveal if clicks come from t.co / m.me which often drop querystring on redirect.

metrics-bot: quick summary (preview): total_clicks=2824, page_views=2701, form_submits=58, conversions_in_pulse=54; top_referrers: t.co(34%), link.ly(22%), facebook.com(18%), direct(10%). last sync: 4812345720.

anya: interesting — t.co is large. but link.ly also shows up. did we accidentally shorten the final landing URL instead of the tracking URL? that can cause utm loss.

felix: i've pulled one shortlink: https://link.ly/xYz9 -> redirects to https://redir.app/s?u=https%3A%2F%2Fredwood.com%2Flaunch%3Futm_source%3Dtwitter%26utm_campaign%3Dmar_launch . the redir.app step strips the querystring. so clicks arrive without utm.

jamie: that explains why Pulseboard attribution falls back to 'direct' and the funnel shows low source conversion. but GA session count still counts because of referrer header. weird split.

metrics-bot: suggested remediation: 1) reprocess inbound_leads_raw for missing utm by joining with click_logs on click_id; 2) mark affected leads with attribution_note="shortlink-utm-loss"; 3) backfill pulseboard. estimated job time ~12m.

raja: can we get the reprocess before monday KPI review? need correct numbers for weekly readout. also flag this as "measurement risk" for the launch.

carmen: will open an ops ticket to stop using link.ly for final URLs and update the campaign doc. i'll also add a banner to the launch pulseboard noting the backfill.

felix: i'll raise a tiny PR to campaign-urls: github.com/redwood/marketing/campaign-urls/pull/7 — change shortlink flow to preserve querystring via redirect param.

anya: please include a short sentence for KPI channel: "Launch session -> conversion gap due to shortlink redirect stripping UTMs; reprocessed +140 leads into campaign attribution; dashboard backfilled." want to keep it high-level.

metrics-bot: reprocess job started by jamie at 4812345802. SQL used (preview): 
```sql
WITH clicks AS (SELECT click_id, original_url FROM click_logs WHERE campaign='mar_launch' AND ts >= '2026-03-23'),
leads AS (SELECT * FROM inbound_leads_raw WHERE path='/launch-2026' AND created_at >= '2026-03-23')
SELECT l.id, c.original_url, parse_qs(c.original_url) as params
FROM leads l LEFT JOIN clicks c ON l.click_id = c.click_id
WHERE (l.utm_source IS NULL OR l.utm_campaign IS NULL);
```

jamie: quick ask — after backfill, can we add a column to weekly KPI export to show "attribution flags" so reviewers can see which cohorts were corrected? helps transparency.

raja: agreed. put it in the KPI playbook update. i'll own the doc change.

metrics-bot: reprocess complete. delta: +140 leads attributed to campaign=mar_launch (most from t.co -> link.ly chain). pulseboard backfilled at 4812345940.

carmen: posted to #kpi: "Launch: shortlink redirect issue caused UTMs to drop for some clicks. +140 leads reattributed to mar_launch; pulseboard updated. see campaign playbook for mitigation."

anya: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) stop link.ly final-target usage (carmen), (2) add attribution_flags export (jamie & raja), (3) add shortlink check to preflight QA for future launches (felix).

felix: noted. will add a preflight checklist item and a unit test for link-building.

jamie: marking this as closed for launch day but will surface in Monday 09:30 KPI review as a short footnote.

raja: reminder: monday KPI readout - include slide 2 updated numbers + attribution footnote.

anya: closing thread. monitoring conversions for rest of day. :rocket:
